newsitem.title: UK: Antarctic inspires composer to write symphony.
newsitem.headline: Antarctic inspires composer to write symphony.

text.p: A leading British composer has been invited to spend one month in the Antarctic by London's Philharmonia Orchestra to help him write a symphony inspired by the continent.

The orchestra said on Monday it had invited Sir Peter Maxwell Davies to write a sequel to Vaughan Williams' Sinfonia Antartica (eds:correct), first performed in 1953 and developed from the score Vaughan Williams wrote for the film "Scott of the Antarctic."

Maxwell Davies, who lives on the remote island of Hoy off the Orkneys in northern Scotland, will later this year visit the Rothera Research Station run by the British Antarctic Survey, which is sharing the commission with the Philharmonia Orchestra.

"Through this commission we hope to raise awareness of Antarctica as a unique scientific laboratory among people whose interests normally lie within the arts," the British Antarctic Survey said in a statement.
"The commission will be announced to our Antarctic wintering staff this weekend as they enjoy the midwinter's day celebrations."
The symphony, Maxwell Davies' eighth, will have its world premiere in 2001, conducted by the composer.
"The Antarctic experience will be an encounter with nature, with silence and emptiness such as one can never experience in Europe, even in remotest Scotland," the 62-year-old composer said.
